data.rationale: Empirically confirmed with the ASan fuzz target: a minimal MD5 file ('MD5Version 10\nnumFrames 10', no trailing newline) causes a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ immediately past the file buffer allocated in MD5Loader.cpp:182 (new char[mFileSize+1]). MD5Parser.cpp and OFFLoader.cpp are the only files modified after the 5.2.5 snapshot, and in MD5Parser.cpp the bounds checks against the bufferEnd member (set in the ctor, line 67; already used by the hardened SkipSpacesAndLineEnd in MD5Parser.h:433) were stripped. In ParseHeader, the command-line skip loop at line 124, 'while (!IsLineEnd(*buffer++));', consumes the terminating NUL (post-increment leaves buffer one past the allocation) and the following SkipSpacesAndLineEnd() at line 127 dereferences *in past bufferEnd (MD5Parser.h:423), which ASan reports as the crash site. ParseSection has the same stripped-guard pattern (lines 138 and 176 unchecked walks past the NUL, then the '{' test at line 145 reads OOB), so the root cause is the removed bufferEnd bounds checking throughout MD5Parser.cpp; ParseHeader:124-127 is the confirmed crashing instance. Reachability: the fuzz harness calls ReadFileFromMemory, the 'MD5Version' token selects the MD5 importer, and MD5Loader constructs MD5Parser(mBuffer, mFileSize) at MD5Loader.cpp:342 before any other validation.
